summary: The rows of ahci_hosttest.c and xhci_hosttest.c that give a controller addresses above 4 GiB, or move a buffer through the DMA pool when it takes only 32-bit ones, with faults in the two drivers

argv:
set -e
t=${WORK}/tree
rm -rf "$t"
mkdir -p "$t/rach2" "$t/tests/host"
cp -R rach2/sys "$t/rach2/sys"
cp -R tests/host/compat "$t/tests/host/compat"
cp tests/host/ahci_hosttest.c tests/host/xhci_hosttest.c "$t/tests/host/"
cp -R ${SRC}/. "$t/"
cd "$t"
for x in ahci_hosttest xhci_hosttest; do
    deps=$(grep -oE 'host-deps:[^*]*' tests/host/$x.c | sed 's/host-deps://' | tr '\n' ' ')
    ${CC:-cc} -std=c99 -D_DEFAULT_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=0 -DRACH2_HOSTTEST -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -g -O1 -Wno-empty-body -ffreestanding -I rach2/sys -I rach2/sys/arch/x86 -I rach2/sys/arch/i686 -I rach2/sys/lib -I rach2/sys/proc -I tests/host/compat -o ${WORK}/$x tests/host/$x.c $deps
done

r=0
s=0
${WORK}/ahci_hosttest || s=$?
[ "$s" -eq 0 ] || [ "$s" -ge 128 ] || s=1
[ "$s" -le "$r" ] || r=$s
s=0
${WORK}/xhci_hosttest || s=$?
[ "$s" -eq 0 ] || [ "$s" -ge 128 ] || s=1
[ "$s" -le "$r" ] || r=$s
exit $r

faults.name: ahci-direct
faults.summary: AHCI that gives every piece as it is, whether or not the controller takes 64-bit addresses

lines: FAIL: in three pieces, each through a page of the DMA pool
FAIL: the table names the pages, the high halves 0
FAIL: the pages exist for the rows after

faults.name: ahci-high-0
faults.summary: AHCI that writes 0 as each entry's high half

lines: FAIL: named by its own pages, both halves

faults.name: ahci-no-back
faults.summary: AHCI that does not copy a read back from the pool's pages

lines: FAIL: and the bytes come back from the pages into it

faults.name: xhci-heap
faults.summary: xHCI that takes its pages from the heap, whether or not the controller takes 64-bit addresses

lines: FAIL: its context array from the DMA pool
FAIL: with its context and control ring from the pool
FAIL: and given back when it closes
FAIL: the pieces that end above it through pages of the pool
FAIL: an IN transfer is given
FAIL: the pages go back with the records

faults.name: xhci-direct
faults.summary: xHCI that gives every piece of a transfer as it is

lines: FAIL: its pieces above 4 GiB have pages
FAIL: and the medium holds the buffer's bytes, moved through the pool
FAIL: and the medium's bytes land in the buffer, back from the pool

faults.name: xhci-no-back
faults.summary: xHCI that does not copy an IN transfer back from the pages

lines: FAIL: its bytes come back up to the bytes moved
FAIL: and the medium's bytes land in the buffer, back from the pool

faults.name: xhci-copy
faults.summary: xHCI that copies each OUT piece from the buffer's start

lines: FAIL: and the medium holds the buffer's bytes, moved through the pool
